answer: Copying the same citations across 172 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 172 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the walnut index resolves every citation against the whisper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the ridge audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 1183 identities would post 1990 proofs and burn roughly 74 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
